phase: Phase A Diagnostics on Existing Data

A1_gar_threshold_audit.n_recent_definition: Total population spike count across all N=500 neurons over the previous 100 ms control step window (Delta_t = 0.1 s).
A1_gar_threshold_audit.formula: Mean Population Firing Rate (Hz) = Spike_Count / (500 neurons * 0.1 s) = Spike_Count / 50

seizure_clamp_code.biological_meaning: Epileptiform hyperactivity threshold (>100 Hz). Correctly set in stimulator.py:56.

seizure_clamp_manuscript_discrepancy.evaluation: ERRONEOUS CLAIM. A threshold of 500 spikes corresponds to 10 Hz. Since nominal network firing is 6.5-14.5 Hz (325-725 spikes), a 500-spike threshold would clamp healthy baseline activity continuously. The code's 5000 threshold (100 Hz) is the genuine epileptiform safeguard.

coma_kick_code.biological_meaning: Quiescence threshold (<1.0 Hz population mean rate). Set in stimulator.py:50.
coma_kick_code.mechanism: Triggers exactly once per episode at step 0 because the 10 ms pre-step integration window generates <50 spikes. Network operates above 1.0 Hz during navigation.

coma_kick_manuscript_discrepancy.evaluation: Text claimed N_recent < 5 (0.1 Hz), whereas stimulator.py implements spike_count < 50 (1.0 Hz).

nan_reset.mechanism: Checks np.any(np.isnan(v)) or np.any(np.isinf(v)) in stimulator.py:27. Resets v=-65, u=0, E=1, I=0.

confound_explanation.root_cause: The DSI evaluation protocol in run_benchmarks_parallel.py:326-337 calls env.step(action_dir), which directly injects I = +25.0 pA current into motor quadrant action_dir via core.py:760-768.
confound_explanation.why_b5_highest_dsi: B5 (random agent) has untrained, weak recurrent connectivity (w_exc ~ 13.08). When +25 pA is injected into a motor quadrant, that quadrant fires at ~20 Hz while un-injected quadrants remain near resting (~2 Hz). Because there is no recurrent excitatory spread, the firing rate disparity is maximal, producing an apparent DSI of 0.678. This is an artifact of isolated current injection into uncoupled neurons, NOT sensory-motor directional tuning.
confound_explanation.why_c0_lower_dsi: C0 (trained model) has grown dense recurrent synaptic connections (w_exc ~ 25.0, w_inh ~ 56.3). When +25 pA is injected into any single quadrant, recurrent excitation rapidly propagates across the entire motor population, causing ALL four quadrants to fire at ~20 Hz. This eliminates quadrant rate disparity (e.g. 20.96 Hz vs 20.24 Hz in seed 42), dropping DSI down to 0.018 in individual seeds and 0.275 overall.
confound_explanation.remedy: Reframe DSI in Section V-C as a descriptive metric of motor population isolation under direct stimulation, explicitly disclosing that untrained networks exhibit higher apparent DSI due to the absence of recurrent excitatory cross-talk.

reward_formulation.exploration_bonus: +0.5 per newly visited grid cell (10x10 grid)
reward_formulation.near_miss_bonus: +1.0 for steering within 0.05 of obstacle without colliding

discrepancy_explanations.c3_vs_c0: Why C3 (no metabolism) has 0.0% goal rate but HIGHER return (-11.05) than C0 (-56.76): In C3, metabolic fatigue is disabled, causing all four motor quadrants to fire continuously at ~20 Hz. This symmetric firing cancels net displacement: dx = 0.05*(N_right - N_left) ~ 0, dy = 0.05*(N_up - N_down) ~ 0. The cursor remains paralyzed near its starting position (0.1, 0.9), completely avoiding the obstacle arena in the center. C3 incurs ZERO obstacle penalties (-15.0/step), accumulating only small step costs (80 * -0.05 = -4.0) and minor shaping drift (-7.0), totaling -11.05. Conversely, C0 actively navigates across the arena (reaching the goal 30.9% of the time with +50 bonuses). However, in the 69% of episodes that fail, bursty motor spikes drive the cursor into obstacles where it becomes trapped for 10-20 steps, accumulating -150 to -300 in penalty points. This heavy left tail pulls C0's mean return down to -56.76.
discrepancy_explanations.c0_vs_b1: Why C0 has HIGHER goal rate (30.9%) than B1 (27.6%) but LOWER return (-56.76 vs +14.65): B1 (direct D3QN on SkeletonEnv) operates with fixed 0.05 kinematic step displacements without SNN burst inertia. When it collides with an obstacle, it can immediately reverse direction without burst latency, spending far fewer steps trapped. Furthermore, SkeletonEnv's reward function omits the full suite of complex shaping terms and maintains stationary dynamics, allowing B1 to achieve a positive net return (+14.65) despite lower goal rate.

return.description: Undiscounted cumulative episode reward over T steps (T <= 80).

goal_rate.description: Fraction of evaluation episodes (episodes 401-500) where final cursor-to-target Euclidean distance is within goal radius.

task_utility_per_1000_spikes.description: Task utility per 1000 spikes. The +250.0 constant is an empirical non-negative offset shift, chosen because episode returns span [-250.0, +100.0]. The shift guarantees non-negative numerators so that higher firing rates appropriately penalize efficiency, avoiding anomalous negative ratios.

directional_selectivity_index.description: Normalized rate contrast across orthogonal motor clusters under 4 cardinal probe commands.

multistep_branching_ratio.description: Wilting & Priesemann (2018) multistep regression estimator of neural avalanche propagation.

avalanche_size_exponent.description: Discrete maximum likelihood power-law exponent (Clauset et al., 2009) for avalanche event sizes S >= 2.

fano_factor.description: Variance-to-mean ratio of population spike counts across temporal bins.

binning_and_subsampling.thresholding: Adaptive activity threshold: 0 spikes/bin, or 35th percentile if active bin fraction > 85%.
binning_and_subsampling.subsampling: 100 motor units (25 per quadrant) out of 500 total network neurons.

A5_seed_audit.finding: AUDIT CONFIRMED: C0 was executed with n=10 seeds [42, 123, 456, 789, 1024, 2024, 3033, 4044, 5055, 6066]. All six ablation conditions (C1-C6) and all five baseline conditions (B1-B5) were executed with n=5 seeds [42, 123, 456, 789, 1024]. The 5 seeds used in ablations and baselines are an exact strict proper subset of the C0 seeds. Equalizing all conditions to n=10 for Phase B requires running the remaining 5 seeds [2024, 3033, 4044, 5055, 6066] across all 11 non-C0 conditions (55 runs).

A6_trujillo_firing_rate_audit.literature_citation: Trujillo et al. (2019) 'Complex Oscillatory Waves Emerging from Cortical Organoids Modeling Early Human Brain Network Development', Cell Stem Cell, 25(4):558-569.

reported_experimental_findings.2_months: < 0.5 Hz spontaneous mean firing rate on HD-MEAs.
reported_experimental_findings.6_to_10_months: 2.0 to 5.0 Hz mean spontaneous resting rate as synchronized oscillatory network activity matures.
reported_experimental_findings.burst_peaks: 10.0 to 20.0 Hz peak firing rates during coordinated population bursts.

A6_trujillo_firing_rate_audit.manuscript_discrepancy: The unrevised manuscript stated: 'physiological resting rates (2-20 Hz)' and 'wet-lab 2-20 Hz human cortical organoid range [Trujillo2019]'. This was an overstatement: human organoids do NOT continuously fire at 20 Hz at rest. The 20 Hz figure represents peak burst rates, while spontaneous resting firing is 2-5 Hz.
A6_trujillo_firing_rate_audit.updated_manuscript_text: We define 2-20 Hz as an adopted operational target band inspired by electrophysiological ranges reported in cortical organoid literature (e.g., Trujillo et al., 2019), where mature spontaneous resting rates span 2-5 Hz and peak synchronous bursts reach 10-20 Hz. In OrganoidEnv, the metabolic governor curtails unconstrained firing, maintaining nominal network activity at 6.51 Hz [5.53, 7.29] within this target band, whereas disabling metabolism (C3) causes firing to escape to 20.61 Hz [18.34, 24.17].

skeleton_env_implementation.kinematics: Fixed step displacement: dx = speed * dir[0], dy = speed * dir[1] with speed = 0.05.

organoid_env_implementation.kinematics: Variable spike-count displacement: dx = 0.05 * (N_right - N_left), dy = 0.05 * (N_up - N_down).
organoid_env_implementation.effective_displacement: Variable integer multiples of 0.05 (e.g., 0.05, 0.10, 0.20, 0.50) depending on motor quadrant spike count.

reward_shaping_discrepancies.waypoint_bonus: Present in OrganoidEnv (+5.0 on crossing halfway mark), absent in SkeletonEnv.
reward_shaping_discrepancies.exploration_bonus: Present in OrganoidEnv (+0.5 per 10x10 cell), absent in SkeletonEnv.
reward_shaping_discrepancies.near_miss_bonus: Present in OrganoidEnv (+1.0 within 0.05 of obstacle), absent in SkeletonEnv.

A7_action_mapping_audit.consequences_and_phase_b_plan: Because OrganoidEnv displacement scales with motor spike bursts, the agent can traverse large distances in few steps, aiding exploration on long corridors (e.g. OOD T4 tight corridor), but also causing severe overshoot into obstacles when motor bursts occur. SkeletonEnv baselines (B1, B2, B4) were restricted to 0.05 fixed steps. In Phase B (Task B4), matched-action baselines will be evaluated.

subthreshold_residuals.comment: Observed subthreshold membrane voltage residual is 1.421e-14 mV, matching Brian2 down to machine double precision.

A8_brian2_cross_check_and_timing.softening_rationale: In subthreshold conditions, the C kernel matches Brian2 to within 1.42e-14 mV. However, in closed-loop recurrent networks with threshold crossings, floating-point rounding at epsilon can trigger a 1-tick shift in spike timing, causing subsequent chaotic trajectory divergence. Therefore, the manuscript claim has been softened from 'bit-exact' to 'numerically cross-checked against Brian2 (maximum subthreshold membrane potential residual 2e-12 mV)'.
